title: FCA charges individual with money laundering
summary: The FCA has charged Raymond Fieldhouse with a money laundering offence. Mr Fieldhouse is accused of laundering over £1.42m made from investment scams between 1 June 2017 and 1 August 2018.Mr Fieldhouse appeared at Stockport Magistrates’ Court on 17 November 2026 where he did not enter a plea. He was remanded in custody until his plea and trial preparation hearing on 22 December 2026 at Southwark Crown Court.Notes to editorsRaymond Fieldhouse was born on 29 April 1982. His nationality is British/Venezuelan. Mr Fieldhouse is accused of money laundering, contrary to section 327 of the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002. Fighting financial crime is a priority in the FCA’s 5-year strategy.The FCA enables a fair and thriving financial services market for the good of consumers and the economy. Find out more about the FCA.

title: Getting the full picture of trading in UK shares
summary: Why a complete picture mattersIn today’s market, firms can choose where and how they trade.Previous analysis has found that this competitive landscape benefits firms in wholesale markets. However, trading in UK shares has become more dispersed across venues and different ways of executing trades. Better information about market-wide activity helps firms assess liquidity, make investment decisions and understand trading costs. However, obtaining a complete picture of that activity has become more difficult.As we set out in CP26/30, overall trading activity in UK equity markets has been robust over recent years (see figure 1).

title: Premature redemption under Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) Scheme - Redemption Price for premature redemption of SGB 2020-21 Series VIII due on November 18, 2026
summary: In terms of GOI notification F.No. 4(4)-B(W&M)/2020 dated October 09, 2020 (SGB 2020-21 Series VIII - Issue date November 18, 2020) on Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme, premature redemption of Gold Bond may be permitted after fifth year from the date of issue of such Gold Bond on the date on which interest is payable. Accordingly, the next due date of premature redemption of the above tranche shall be on November 18, 2026. 2. Further, the redemption price of SGB shall be based on simple average of closing price of gold of 999 purity of previous three business days from the date of redemption, as published by the India Bullion and Jewellers Association Ltd (IBJA). Accordingly, the redemption price for premature redemption due on November 18, 2026, shall be ₹13,499/- (Rupees Thirteen Thousand Four Hundred and Ninety-Nine Only) per unit of SGB based on the simple average of closing price of gold for the three business days i.e., November 13, November 16, and November 17, 2026. Ajit Prasad Deputy General Manager (Communications) Press Release: 2026-2027/1512

title: Directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 – Nagar Sahakari Bank Ltd., Etawah – Extension of Period
summary: The Reserve Bank of India issued Directions under Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 to Nagar Sahakari Bank Ltd., Etawah, vide Directive No. LKO.DOS.SED.No.S29/12-03-000/2026-2027 dated May 15, 2026, for a period of six months up to close of business on November 18, 2026. The Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of operation of the Directive beyond close of business on November 18, 2026. 2. Accordingly, the Reserve Bank of India, in the exercise of the powers vested in it under sub-section (1) of Section 35A read with Section 56 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, hereby extends the Directive for a further period of three months from close of business on November 18, 2026, to close of business on February 18, 2027, subject to review. 3. The aforesaid extension and/or modification by the Reserve Bank of India should not per se be construed to imply that the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied with the financial position of the bank. 4. All other terms and conditions of the Directive under reference, shall remain unchanged. (Brij Raj) Chief General Manager Press Release: 2026-202

title: New trade-restrictive measures surge but WTO members step up trade facilitation efforts
summary: The pace of newly-introduced tariffs and other non-facilitating measures rose sharply in the first half of 2026, while the stockpile of such measures reached a record level, according to the WTO Director-General's latest annual overview of developments in the international trading environment. At the same time, WTO members introduced a significant number of trade-facilitating measures, helping to sustain global trade flows despite heightened geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainty.
